gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-labrada: Chunky, unfinished-looking bowls and strokes that never swell or thin: that is Comic Relief up top, with Labrada below it. Its text serif is dignified and bookish.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-laila: Laila reads like a traditional editorial serif, with generous gaps where its curves meet the stems. Comic Relief above it is the loud, uniform-stroked one.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-montaga: Comic Relief is the blunt, bold voice here, strokes the same all the way round and bowls left open on one side. Montaga is the bookish serif, its curves lifted off like stitched thread.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-new-tegomin: Loud and plain-stroked on top, with bowls left open. New Tegomin follows in a dignified serif whose wide ring of a c suggests giving it a touch more size than the heading.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-podkova: Podkova reads as a bookish, traditional serif, its c opening broad and welcoming. And Comic Relief's stiff, same-thickness capitals above it make a long page feel friendly and unhurried.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-rhodium-libre: No tilt in Comic Relief's round letters, just bold, commanding strokes. Rhodium Libre below is an editorial classic serif with brush ends lifting away before each curve closes, which gives a long read a traditional, handwritten warmth.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-sanchez: Comic Relief cuts every stroke to one depth, like an engraver, with bowls left open on one side. But Sanchez is the bookish text serif, its c spread like calipers, and that gap is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-solway: Comic Relief hits hard, with bowls left unfinished and no difference between up and side strokes. And Solway answers as an authoritative serif, flat in line weight and generous at the e's eye.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-yuji-boku: Every stroke of Comic Relief is cut at one weight, and its bowls stay open on one side. Yuji Boku, a dignified classic serif, is the counterweight.
